summary_html: Federal transparency statutes—**FOIA** and **Sunshine Act**—require disclosure of government data. Project Milk Carton promotes FOIA requests and public dashboards for child-welfare records.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: Beattie v. Aiken County Department of Social Services
key_cases.holding: The court held that parents whose case was closed as unfounded may not examine the DSS case file, that 'report' covers all investigative information and the reporter's identity is never disclosable, and that FOIA requires separation and release of non-exempt material where a court is asked to conduct that review.
key_cases.relevance: Beattie is the pivotal case for any FOIA request to DSS: closed-by-law records fall outside FOIA, but exempt and non-exempt material must be separated.
key_cases.quote: The clear language of § 20-7-650 prohibits the disclosure of the DSS case file to Appellants or to anyone else.

key_cases.case_name: Disabato v. South Carolina Ass'n of School Administrators
key_cases.holding: The court held that applying the South Carolina FOIA to a nonprofit corporation supported in part by public funds does not violate its First Amendment speech and association rights, and reversed dismissal of the FOIA action.
key_cases.relevance: Disabato is the leading modern South Carolina FOIA decision on who counts as a public body and what interests can justify withholding.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that while the FOIA does impact upon SCASA's speech and association rights, the First Amendment is not violated.

key_cases.case_name: Newberry Publishing Co. v. Newberry County Commission on Alcohol & Drug Abuse
key_cases.holding: The court reversed, holding that no criminal investigative report is per se exempt under the South Carolina FOIA and that a public body must separate exempt from non-exempt material and release the non-exempt portion, with exemption decided on a case-by-case basis.
key_cases.relevance: It forbids a blanket policy of denying records requests for investigative files and is the controlling South Carolina authority on segregating exempt from non-exempt material in response to a FOIA request.
key_cases.quote: a public record containing both nonexempt and exempt material must be segregated so that the nonexempt material is made available to the public

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The Fourth Circuit reversed, holding that the confidential retention of records of a child abuse investigation classified 'unsubstantiated' and 'ruled out' violates neither substantive nor procedural due process, so the state officials were entitled to qualified immunity.
key_cases.relevance: It catalogues the legitimate state interests — pattern detection, avoiding repeat investigations, defending suits alleging inadequate investigation — that justify retaining exactly the records a transparency request would seek.
key_cases.quote: The record before us presents no substantive due process violation of a familial privacy liberty interest by virtue of the retention of the Hodge investigation report
